Let's dive into Chapter 5: Public Visibility—How Making Things Observable Fuels Imitation and Spread.
So far, we’ve talked about social currency, triggers, and emotion—why we share, and when. But have you ever wondered how certain things seem to catch on just because everyone can see them? That’s where public visibility comes in.
Think about the last time you passed a busy restaurant with a line stretching out the door. You might not have known a thing about the food, but seeing all those people waiting was a pretty strong signal, right? That visible crowd tells you, “Hey, this place must be good!” And just like that, you might find yourself tempted to join the line, too.
Public visibility acts almost like a living, breathing social billboard. When what we do or use is out in the open, it’s an open invitation for others to notice—and often, to copy. That’s why trends, like a certain sneaker or a particular style of coffee cup, seem to spread so quickly. When enough people are seen wearing or using something, it sends a clear message: “This is what’s in.”
Some products are naturally set up for this. Picture a laptop with a bold logo, a reusable mug with a bright design, or those charity wristbands that were everywhere for a while. All of these make it easy for others to spot what you’re using, making imitation almost effortless.
But here’s the flip side—not everything is out in the open. Some things, like a behind-the-scenes software tool, stay hidden. If people can’t see it, they’re less likely to pick up on it, and the spread slows down.
So, how do you make your product or idea stand out in public? It starts with design—add a unique logo, a signature color, or a distinct shape. Or, encourage people to use your product where others can see. Maybe offer little rewards for showing off their achievements or participation.
For example, companies often design products with easily recognizable features, set up public demos, or create badges and stickers that people can display. All of these small touches make it easier for others to spot and then join in.
There’s also a really interesting feedback loop here. When people see something that boosts their social currency, and it’s visible, they want to share it even more. The more it’s seen, the more it spreads.
And in the digital world, this effect is even stronger. Social media makes public visibility instant—one post, like, or share can be seen by hundreds or thousands of people in seconds. That’s why some ideas or trends go viral almost overnight.
So, here’s the key takeaway: If you want your idea, product, or behavior to spread, make it easy for people to see. When something’s out in the open, folks are much more likely to imitate and share it, helping your idea catch on and take off.
